findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` (unlike `disconnectMutation` on lines 61-64). Because `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` queries `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.useQuery` with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and its callers do not always pass an `onChanged` callback that refetches this query, `cacheUpdatedAt` remains stale in the React Query cache after deletion and the dropdown continues showing the old cache status and the "Delete cached data" action until the page is reloaded.

findings.title: `connectedCalendarsHandler` bypasses `CalendarCache.init` feature-flag check
findings.body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` directly instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of calling `await CalendarCache.init(null)`. `CalendarCache.init` checks whether the `calendar-cache` feature is enabled and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when it is disabled. Instantiating `CalendarCacheRepository` directly bypasses the feature flag, leaves `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` unused, and runs `calendarCache.groupBy` queries and exposes cache status UI even when `calendar-cache` is disabled.

findings.title: Unused `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` writes and session payload fields
findings.body: `CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to touch `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` (in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`, lines 899-900) selects `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every `SelectedCalendar` during session loading. Because the feature now reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, these `SelectedCalendar` fields are unused, causing an unnecessary `UPDATE` on all selected calendars on every cache refresh and enlarging the session user payload.

findings.title: Relative `.env` path and macOS-only `sed -i ''` break script when run from repo root or on Linux
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script's directory (`$(dirname "$0")/..`), so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root creates/modifies `../.env` outside the repository. In addition, `sed -i '' -E` on line 68 uses BSD/macOS `sed` syntax and fails on Linux where GNU `sed` treats `''` as an input filename.
